records.body:
## Safe diagnostic sequence

1. Copy the exact command, exit status, and concise error message.
2. Confirm the current project root and active installation path.
3. Check whether the affected file is user-owned, linked, generated, or
   manifest-managed.
4. Run the narrowest documented diagnostic or test.
5. Escalate to repair only after understanding what state it may discard.

## Complete recovery reference

If help reports a missing or malformed installation catalog, preserve local
changes and follow the normal [update path](../versioning.md). Maintainers
refresh the catalog through `python scripts/cg_generate_targets.py --all`;

records.heading: Choose the problem
records.body:
## Choose the problem

For source-cited guidance, ask `/cg-help` in chat, for example
`/cg-help compare planning and work`. Help is advisory: it does not activate
suites, repair installations, or execute the recommended commands. It asks for
clarification when needed and reports unsupported requests instead of inventing
an answer. Ask in your preferred language; command identifiers remain unchanged.

From a terminal on Windows or macOS, use the installed wrapper:

```text
cg-help query "How do I configure this project?" --root "/path/to/project" --format json
```

On Windows use a Windows path, such as `--root "E:\my project"`. The catalog
and cited sources belong to the plugin installation, so consumers need no local
`docs/` or `scripts/`. Help distinguishes active commands from inactive suites;
before setup or with invalid configuration, it labels general setup guidance
without claiming verified command availability. Inactive commands receive
metadata and a remedy, not their workflow instructions.

# Installation

This detailed page covers platform-specific installation, linking, repair, and
uninstall procedures. New users should follow the shorter
[Getting Started](getting-started/index.md) path first.

Existing users on any older version, pinned or tracking `latest`: follow [Upgrade from an older version](upgrade.md) before running installed update or link commands, and keep the resulting release pin.

> **New here?** See the [Home](../README.md) page for an overview of what Compound GPID is and why it exists.

**Platform**: Jump to your operating system:
- [Windows installation](#windows-installation)
- [macOS installation](#macos-installation)

Both installers register the committed `cg-help` wrapper alongside the existing
commands (`cg-help.cmd` on Windows). After restarting the terminal, run
`cg-help query "How do I configure this project?" --root "<project path>" --format json`.
Use a real Windows path such as `E:\my project`, or a macOS path such as
`/Users/me/my project`. Python 3.8+ is required; Windows Store stubs are rejected.
The [help guide](help/index.md) explains active/inactive selection, labelled
pre-setup guidance, source citations, unsupported requests, and catalog refresh.
The consumer does not need its own `docs/` or `scripts/`; evidence comes from the
plugin installation. Help never installs, configures, or repairs anything.

records.heading: Step 4 - Configure your project (once per project)
records.body:
## Step 4 - Configure your project (once per project)

Open your project in VS Code and run in Copilot Chat:

```
/cg-setup
```

> ⚠️ **Do not skip this step.** `/cg-setup` creates the `.cg-docs/` directory structure (brainstorms, plans, reviews, strategy, solutions, archive) required by all workflow prompts. If you skip it, `/cg-strategy`, `/cg-review`, and `/cg-compound` will fail to write their output artifacts.

This configures language preferences, project type, review depth, and active
suites, scaffolds the `.cg-docs/` directory,
and creates three config files:

- `compound-gpid.local.md` — always created and committed; shared team config (language, review depth, and `suites: [cg]`, `[cr]`, or `[cg, cr]`)
- `compound-gpid.md` — optional; committed; shared project charter (objective, deliverables, constraints, current focus). All `/cg-*` prompts read this automatically.
- `compound-gpid.context.md` — optional; committed; a growing knowledge base for project-specific facts Copilot can consult when needed (data sources, variable caveats, workspace folder descriptions, domain vocabulary). Ordinary prompts load targeted headings or snippets instead of reading the whole file by default. Grows over time via `/cg-compound`.

> **Existing repos**: If your project already has code (R, Python, Stata, etc.), `/cg-setup` will dispatch `@cg-project-scanner` to scan the file tree first. The scanner infers language, project type, and a charter draft from existing signals — you only confirm or correct what it found. High-confidence detections are set silently; medium-confidence ones are pre-filled and shown for confirmation. You can skip the charter entirely and create `compound-gpid.md` later by re-running `/cg-setup`.

> **Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Kilo support**: Compound GPID generates native
> platform trees (`.claude/`, `.agents/`, `.opencode/`, `.kilo/`) from the
> canonical `.github/` source. `cg-link` links them by default; pass `--platforms`
> to narrow the target set. The legacy `adapters/` directory contains
> opt-in source adapters that are superseded by the generated trees but remain
> for backward compatibility.
>
> Each linked skill is an atomic bundle: `SKILL.md` and all nested regular
> support files are included by default. Executable resources are opaque files;
> packaging preserves their mode but never executes them. See
> [Generated Native Platform Trees](context-files.md#generated-native-platform-trees).

> **Kilo parser diagnostics**: malformed managed Kilo skill, agent, and `cg-*`
> command frontmatter is reported as a local-content failure. Kilo's own
> schema-validation failure is reported separately from external skill
> discovery; one must not be used as evidence for the other.

> **Suite selection**: `/cg-setup` records active suites in
> `compound-gpid.local.md`. An absent `suites:` field defaults to `[cg]` for
> backward compatibility. For configured consumers, suites and capabilities
> determine the active manifest and project-local runtime projection. The global
> generated trees remain the shared source baseline. Maintainers can request an isolated filtered build
> with `--active-suites`. See the [Modular Guide](modular-guide.md).

---
prerequisites: > **Requirements**: Windows 10/11, PowerShell 5.1+, git, **Python 3.8+**.

> Python is required by `cg-skill`, the `cg-index` knowledge indexer, the `cg-token-audit` context/model audit, and the repo-local summary tools. Install from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/) or via winget: `winget install Python.Python.3.11`. The Windows Store Python stub is not sufficient — install real Python and ensure `python`, `python3`, or `py` is on your PATH. If Python is not installed, `install.ps1` will stop with an error and print install instructions. See [Python not found](troubleshooting.md#python-not-found) in Troubleshooting if you run into issues.

> ⚠️ **Do not skip this step.** `/cg-setup` creates the `.cg-docs/` directory structure (brainstorms, plans, reviews, strategy, solutions, archive) required by all workflow prompts. If you skip it, `/cg-strategy`, `/cg-review`, and `/cg-compound` will fail to write their output artifacts.

records.heading: macOS installation
records.body:
## macOS installation

> **Requirements**: macOS 12 (Monterey) or later, bash (pre-installed), git, **Python 3.8+**.
> macOS often provides `python3` through Xcode Command Line Tools. Compound GPID probes `python3`, then `python`, then `py` and accepts the first command whose `--version` output starts with `Python`. If none is on your PATH, run `xcode-select --install` or install Python from python.org/Homebrew.
prerequisites: > **Requirements**: macOS 12 (Monterey) or later, bash (pre-installed), git, **Python 3.8+**.

records.heading: Step 1 — Clone (once per machine)
records.body:
### Step 1 — Clone (once per machine)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/GPID-WB/compound-gpid.git ~/.compound-gpid
```

You can substitute any path you prefer, e.g. `~/tools/.compound-gpid`. The scripts are fully location-agnostic.
prerequisites: > **Requirements**: macOS 12 (Monterey) or later, bash (pre-installed), git, **Python 3.8+**.

records.heading: Step 2 — Install (once per machine)
records.body:
### Step 2 — Install (once per machine)

```bash
bash ~/.compound-gpid/scripts/install.sh
```

This:
- Registers the committed executable wrappers (`cg-link`, `cg-unlink`, `cg-update`, `cg-skill`, `cg-index`, `cg-brain-init`, `cg-render-artifact`, `cg-publish-markdown`, `cg-token-audit`) in `~/.compound-gpid/bin/`; Python 3.8+ provides skill lifecycle management, Brainstorm/Plan validation, HTML rendering, and generic Markdown publication with the `reference` theme, and the same `bin/` directory also contains repo-local summary wrappers such as `cg-test-summary`, `cg-diff-summary`, `cg-log-summary`, `cg-tree-summary`, and `cg-problems-summary`. The installer does not rewrite or chmod wrappers; missing or non-executable wrappers stop installation with re-clone guidance.
- Adds that directory to your PATH via `~/.zshrc` (or `~/.bashrc` for bash users)
- Creates `.cg-version` with `latest` only when absent; preserves an existing version preference

> ⚠️ **IMPORTANT — After install, restart your terminal and VS Code / Positron:**
> - **Terminal restart**: the PATH change only takes effect in new processes.
> - **VS Code / Positron restart**: Copilot must re-index the workspace to pick up new commands.
prerequisites: > **Requirements**: macOS 12 (Monterey) or later, bash (pre-installed), git, **Python 3.8+**.
warnings: - Creates `.cg-version` with `latest` only when absent; preserves an existing version preference

records.heading: Step 3 — Link your project (once per project)
records.body:
### Step 3 — Link your project (once per project)

From your project root:

```bash
cg-link
```

This links Compound GPID install units for all supported platforms by default: GitHub Copilot (`.github/`), Claude Code (`.claude/`), Codex (`.agents/`), OpenCode (`.opencode/`), and Kilo (`.kilo/`). For projects with `compound-gpid.local.md`, native runtime directories and Copilot skills are managed project-local projections; other Copilot directory units are symlinks on macOS. Projects without that config use legacy directory links, with managed copies for Kilo. Strict config/root-adapter files use ownership checks, so existing user-owned files are preserved.

> **Platform selection**: To install only specific platforms:
> ```bash
> cg-link --platforms copilot
> cg-link --platforms kilo
> cg-link --platforms copilot,claude-code,codex,opencode,kilo
> ```
> Default (`cg-link` with no flag) links all supported platforms.

> With Kilo and Codex/Claude roots present, launch Kilo only through
> `cg-kilo`. The contained launcher is the supported containment boundary;
> direct editor/CLI launches are intentionally unsupported by the coexistence
> policy. Install, update, and link do not require Kilo or host certification;
> the optional launcher's version diagnostics produce warnings only.

> ⚠️ **IMPORTANT — Restart VS Code / Positron after linking.**
> Copilot must re-index the workspace to see the newly linked prompts, skills, and agents.

The legacy `adapters/` directory contains opt-in source adapters that are
superseded by the generated native trees but remain for backward compatibility.

records.heading: macOS — Updating
records.body:
### macOS — Updating

```bash
cg-update
```

This uses the installation's saved `.cg-version` preference: a pin stays on its selected tag, while `latest` pulls the branch. Normal updates refuse tracked or staged user edits rather than discarding them. Linked directory units reflect installation changes immediately; copies and projections need the [consumer refresh](#refreshing-existing-consumer-projects) steps below.

**Version pinning**: the same pinning commands work on macOS:

```bash
cg-update --list       # browse three-component release tags
cg-update v1.2.0.9024  # pin to a specific release
cg-update latest      # return to tracking main
```

Version preference is stored in `~/.compound-gpid/.cg-version` (or your chosen install path). See [Version Management](versioning.md) for full details.

records.heading: Refreshing existing consumer projects
records.body:
### Refreshing existing consumer projects

The root `.compound-gpid-source.json` marker belongs only to the Compound GPID
source checkout. It is not projected or installed in consumer projects.

- **Legacy links**: run `cg-update`. Existing directory links receive the fixed
  command immediately. Run `cg-link --platforms <platforms>` only to recreate or
  repair old links.
- **Kilo managed copies**: rerun `cg-link --platforms <platforms>` from the
  consumer project to refresh runtime directory copies. Use the intended full
  platform list (`kilo` only for a Kilo-only project); `cg-update` alone does not
  queue those legacy directories for copying.
- **Manifest projections**: `cg-update` verifies and syncs the existing active
  manifest, but does not change its immutable selection. A changed installation
  revision, platform selection, or other stale manifest input requires
  `cg-link --platforms <platforms>` to resolve a fresh manifest before syncing.
  Preserve the intended full platform list and review `cg-link --check` and any
  manual-action diagnostics rather than bypassing ownership checks.

Restart VS Code or Positron after a refresh so the host reloads command files.

---

records.heading: Version Pinning
records.body:
## Version Pinning

By default `cg-update` tracks `main` and always pulls the latest commit. If you need stability (or want to try a beta), you can pin to a specific [GitHub Release](https://github.com/GPID-WB/compound-gpid/releases).

> **`latest` is a keyword**, not a version number. It means "track `main` and always pull the newest commit" — it does **not** refer to the newest numbered release. `cg-update --list` shows three-component release tags only; four-component tags such as `v1.2.0.9024` require an explicit version argument.
prerequisites: > **`latest` is a keyword**, not a version number. It means "track `main` and always pull the newest commit" — it does **not** refer to the newest numbered release. `cg-update --list` shows three-component release tags only; four-component tags such as `v1.2.0.9024` require an explicit version argument.

records.heading: Browse available releases
records.body:
### Browse available releases

```bash
cg-update --list
```

Fetches tag metadata and displays three-component release tags, with your current version marked if it is listed. A four-component pin is shown in the current-mode label but omitted from the table.

records.heading: Pin to a specific release
records.body:
### Pin to a specific release

```bash
cg-update v1.2.0.9024
```

Checks out that release tag, validates its required scripts and generated targets, then writes `v1.2.0.9024` to `.cg-version` in your install directory. Subsequent bare `cg-update` calls stay on this version.
prerequisites: Checks out that release tag, validates its required scripts and generated targets, then writes `v1.2.0.9024` to `.cg-version` in your install directory. Subsequent bare `cg-update` calls stay on this version.

records.heading: Return to tracking main
records.body:
### Return to tracking main

```bash
cg-update latest
```

Unpins and resumes pulling `main` on every `cg-update` call.

> **Version preference is per-machine.** It is stored in `.cg-version` inside your global install directory:
> - **Windows**: `C:\WBG\.compound-gpid\.cg-version` or `$env:USERPROFILE\.compound-gpid\.cg-version`
> - **macOS**: `~/.compound-gpid/.cg-version` (or your chosen install path)
>
> This file is gitignored and never committed — each machine keeps its own preference independently.

> **Full details on version management**: see the dedicated [Version Management](versioning.md) page for command output examples, when to use each mode, multi-machine scenarios, and troubleshooting.

records.heading: Repairing a broken installation
records.body:
## Repairing a broken installation

Before repairing, back up the entire installation, including untracked files,
local commits, and `.cg-version`. Inspect the clone and record the intended
version without changing it:

**macOS:**
```bash
cg="$HOME/.compound-gpid"   # adjust if you chose a different install path
git -C "$cg" status --short
git -C "$cg" log -1 --oneline
cat "$cg/.cg-version"
```

**Windows:**
```powershell
# Uncomment your install path:
$cg = "C:\WBG\.compound-gpid"              # local machine (OneDrive)
# $cg = "$env:USERPROFILE\.compound-gpid"    # remote server
git -C $cg status --short
git -C $cg log -1 --oneline
Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $cg ".cg-version")
```

Move conflicting untracked files to a reviewed backup and preserve tracked
edits outside the managed clone before retrying `cg-update` with the same
version preference. If the pin is missing or corrupted, follow
[pin recovery](troubleshooting.md#cg-version-missing-or-corrupted). If the clone
has diverged or needs replacement, keep it intact and use the fresh-clone
procedure in the upgrade guide linked at the top of this page; do not reset it to `origin/main`.

`cg-update --fix` is a destructive opt-in, not a safe default repair: it removes
untracked files, discards tracked edits, then runs `git pull --ff-only`. It does
not switch a detached tag checkout to a branch, so it is unsuitable for pinned
installations. Use it only on a branch with an upstream after deliberately
choosing to discard those files and keeping a complete backup. It is not a
migration path for an older installation.

After recovery, follow the consumer refresh steps above for each linked project.

> **Existing projects — `.cg-docs/strategy/`**: If you linked your project before this release, create the strategy folder manually:
> ```powershell
> New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .cg-docs\strategy | Out-Null
> New-Item -ItemType File -Force .cg-docs\strategy\.gitkeep | Out-Null
> ```

> **Migrating from an old install path?** If you previously installed to `$env:USERPROFILE\.compound-gpid` on a local OneDrive machine, see [Upgrading from an old installation](troubleshooting.md#upgrading-from-envuserprofilecompound-gpid-old-default-path-local-onedrive-machines-only) in the Troubleshooting page.

---

> **Having trouble?** Check the [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) page for known issues and fixes.

records.heading: Step 3 - Link your project (once per project)
records.body:
## Step 3 - Link your project (once per project)

From your project root:

```powershell
cg-link
```

This links Compound GPID install units for all supported platforms by default: GitHub Copilot (`.github/`), Claude Code (`.claude/`), Codex (`.agents/`), OpenCode (`.opencode/`), and Kilo (`.kilo/`). For projects with `compound-gpid.local.md`, native runtime directories and Copilot skills are managed project-local projections; other Copilot directory units are junctions on Windows. Projects without that config use legacy directory links, with managed copies for Kilo. Strict config/root-adapter files use ownership checks, so existing user-owned files are preserved.

> **Platform selection**: To install only specific platforms, pass `--platforms`:
> ```powershell
> cg-link --platforms copilot
> cg-link --platforms kilo
> cg-link --platforms copilot,claude-code,codex,opencode,kilo
> ```
> Default (`cg-link` with no flag) links all supported platforms. See [Context
> Files](context-files.md) for details on generated native platform trees.

To inspect the current project before linking, run `cg-link --check`. Use
`cg-link --check --platforms kilo` to limit the report. The report uses the
current local installation, resolves desired selection and output in memory,
and lists each relevant path's owner, current state, action that `cg-link`
would take, and reason. Items that need manual action are listed separately.
It never runs `cg-update`, Kilo, or a publication/recovery step, and does not
write project files, state, `.gitignore`, HOME configuration, or caches.
Python runs with `-B`. Compatibility mirrors under
`.compound-gpid/kilo-compat-skills` and their links are assessed with existing
copy receipts and checksums. Recognized managed links need no manual action;
modified mirror files and foreign links are preserved for review.
Related permission/plugin entries in `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc` are
**INFORMATION ONLY**. They never block and are never written by `--check`.
Unreadable or invalid global settings are reported, not repaired.
Missing or old output alone is not a blocker. Exit codes
are `0` for a nonblocking report, `1` for a block or preserved conflict, and `2`
for invalid usage. Unknown options are rejected with usage before any update
or write, including when `--check` or `--help` is also present.
The report uses the same checksum-based Copilot instruction ownership policy as
linking, including its one-time backed-up legacy transition.

> **Kilo + Codex/Claude coexistence**: when a project contains Kilo plus a
> Codex or Claude skill root, direct Kilo editor/CLI launches are unsupported.
> Run the contained launcher `cg-kilo` from the project root. It performs the
> local projection and containment checks, then sets
> `KILO_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS=1` only for the child Kilo process. It does not
> modify global Kilo configuration or the caller's environment. These optional
> launcher checks do not run as lifecycle host gates. Install, update, and link
> still validate managed files without depending on Kilo host behavior.

There is **no minimum or certified Kilo version requirement** for install,
update, link, or `cg-kilo`. Old or unreadable `--version` output produces a
warning only; it does not prevent executable selection or a contained launch.
The launcher still blocks invalid local projections, failed host commands or
schemas, missing local skills, and ineffective containment. Recorded CI
versions and executable hashes identify tested binaries, not consumer version
requirements.

Older installed lifecycle scripts can still contain obsolete Kilo version
gates. Follow the migration instructions for your installed release to obtain
the new scripts. Do not set `CG_INTERNAL_CALL`, disable containment, downgrade
Kilo, or edit an existing release tag to avoid an obsolete version gate.

> ⚠️ **IMPORTANT — Restart VS Code / Positron after linking.**
> Copilot must re-index the workspace to see the newly linked prompts, skills, and agents.
> Without a restart, `/cg-setup` and other prompts will not be available.

> **Junction errors**: Windows directory junctions do not require Developer Mode.
> Check the reported path, permissions, filesystem support, and conflicting files.

> **Managed vs. user-owned files**: files inside linked directories (`prompts/`, `skills/`, `commands/`, `agents/`, etc.) are managed by Compound GPID - do not edit them directly. `copilot-instructions.md` uses checksum receipts: unchanged managed files may be refreshed, while modified files are preserved. An unreceipted legacy file with the `<!-- compound-gpid:managed -->` marker can undergo a one-time replacement only after its original bytes are saved to `.github/copilot-instructions.md.pre-9024.bak`; an existing backup blocks that transition. Review and merge custom instructions from the backup. Strict JSON config files such as `.opencode/opencode.json` also use `.compound-gpid/managed-files.json` checksums; `cg-update` refreshes them only if they are unmodified. If a user-owned config exists, `cg-link` skips it and prints a manual snippet.
>
> The consumer `.compound-gpid/managed-files.json` is separate from the
> `.compound-gpid-generated.json` manifests committed inside the upstream
> `.claude/`, `.agents/`, `.opencode/`, and `.kilo/` trees. Consumers should not
> copy, edit, or use generated-tree manifests to resolve installation ownership.

> Python is required by `cg-skill`, the `cg-index` knowledge indexer, the `cg-token-audit` context/model audit, and the repo-local summary tools. Install from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/) or via winget: `winget install Python.Python.3.11`. records.heading: Workflow Overview
records.body:
# Workflow Overview

Choose the shortest workflow that matches the uncertainty and risk of the task.
Commands are workflow entry points; skills and most agents are loaded by those
commands rather than invoked directly.

New to the standard module? Start with the [module introduction](standard.md),
then follow [your first workflow](first-workflow.md) or adapt a [use case](examples.md).

records.heading: Choose by situation
records.body:
## Choose by situation

First choose the suite that owns the task. Use `/cg-*` for technical delivery,
infrastructure, and code-review workflows. Use `/cr-*` for research scoping,
identification, measurement, econometrics, replication, writing, and
publication output. The research suite composes shared implementation
capabilities without depending on the technical command suite.

For a guided first research workflow, use the [Research Handbook](../research/index.md).

records.heading: The standard loop
records.body:
## The standard loop

```text
Understand -> Plan -> Deliver -> Assure -> Resolve -> Remember
```

```text
/cg-brainstorm -> /cg-plan -> /cg-work -> /cg-review -> /cg-fix-triage -> /cg-compound
```

`/cg-light-work` is only for a qualified small technical task. Its first user
gate approves a saved Plan before source edits. It then writes a Work Report and
Review Report, runs the fixed mandatory light Review with `@cg-code-quality` and
`@cg-testing`, and permits one initial pass plus one verification pass only when
Review fixes changed files. Its second user gate is explicit compounding opt-in;
skip creates no permanent knowledge side effect.

Reproducible bugs use `/cg-fixbug`. Research, statistical, and publication work
uses `/cr-*`. Larger, ambiguous, security-sensitive, schema, dependency, or
destructive work uses `/cg-brainstorm` -> `/cg-plan` -> `/cg-work`. `/cg-work`
executes approved saved Plans and redirects unmatched inline tasks without
dispatching them.
